In this Internship, you will work on the technical infrastructure behind our revenue engine.


You will work directly with our Sales, Customer Success, Marketing, Operations, and Product teams to identify bottlenecks, build internal tools, automate workflows, connect systems, and deploy AI where it creates measurable commercial impact.


Role description

What You’ll Do

Work on our GTM operating system

  • Build the systems powering our entire customer lifecycle – from first lead to closed customer and expansion.

  • Build internal applications and workflows that help SDRs, Account Executives, Customer Success Managers, and leadership make better decisions and execute faster.

  • Turn fragmented processes into scalable systems.


Automate the revenue engine

  • Identify repetitive or inefficient workflows across Sales, Marketing, and Customer Success and automate them.

  • Build automations for areas such as lead enrichment, routing, qualification, follow-ups, pipeline management, customer onboarding, and retention.

  • Connect our GTM stack and ensure information moves reliably between systems.


Integrate AI into real workflows

  • Move AI beyond prototypes.

  • Build AI-powered workflows that help us qualify and prioritize leads, analyze calls and customer interactions, identify opportunities and risks, generate insights, and automate operational work.

  • Experiment rapidly with new models and tools and turn successful experiments into reliable internal products.


Build, don’t just recommend

  • You will personally implement what you design.

  • Depending on the problem, that might mean writing Python or TypeScript, building an n8n workflow, connecting an API, querying a database, prototyping an internal application, or working with our engineers on a deeper integration.

  • You should be comfortable moving between commercial conversations and technical implementation.


Drive measurable commercial impact

  • Technology is a means, not the outcome.

  • Your work should ultimately help us generate more pipeline, increase conversion, shorten sales cycles, improve retention, or allow our GTM organization to scale without adding unnecessary complexity.

  • You will work closely with GTM leadership to identify the highest-leverage problems and own them from idea to measurable result.


Requirements

  • You are a builder. When you see a broken process, your instinct is to understand it and build something better.

  • You have strong technical skills and have worked in Python and/or TypeScript

  • You have hands-on experience building automations and integrations using tools such as n8n and APIs

  • You are comfortable working with databases, APIs, webhooks, and data pipelines

  • You are interested in Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, and the systems behind how SAAS companies create revenue 

  • You can translate an ambiguous business problem into a technical solution without needing a detailed specification

  • You move fast, iterate, and are comfortable shipping a first version before everything is perfect

  • You are fluent in English. German or another European language is a plus


Bonus Points

  • You have first experience in a dynamic start-up environment and have worked on technical solutions

  • Tools like HubSpot, Aircall, Stripe, Intercom, PostHog, or similar platforms are not entirely new for you

  • Ideally you have worked on or build internal tools, AI agents, lead-scoring systems, enrichment pipelines, or automated outbound workflows.

  • You have worked in an early-stage or high-growth startup where speed and ownership mattered more than clearly defined responsibilities.

Du machst diese Marken in klassischer Suche und in generativen Systemen sichtbar. Der Hebel dafür ist Content: Sichtbarkeit entsteht heute über Inhalte, die Suchintention treffen und zitierfähig sind, nicht über Keyword-Dichte. Du gibst die inhaltliche Richtung vor und sorgst dafür, dass die Sichtbarkeit belegbar ist, nicht behauptet.

  • Strategie über die gesamte Suchlandschaft: Du entwickelst Search- und Content-Strategien, die klassisches SEO und GEO/AI Search zusammenführen, statt sie als zwei Projekte zu behandeln. Du priorisierst nach Impact, nicht nach Vollständigkeit.
  • Technisches SEO in der Tiefe: Crawling, Indexierung, Core Web Vitals, JS-Rendering, Logfile-Analyse, internes Verlinkungs- und Informationsdesign. Du begleitest Relaunches und Migrationen so, dass danach nicht die Sichtbarkeit fehlt.
  • Content-Strategie und Entitätsarchitektur: Du entwickelst Themen-, Content- und Entitätsarchitekturen entlang der B2B Buying Journey von Awareness-Content für die frühe Recherche bis zu Deep-Content, aus dem LLMs zitieren. Du entscheidest, welche Themen besetzt werden, welche Formate es braucht und was bestehender Content leisten muss.
  • Content steuern, nicht schreiben: Du briefst unser Content-Team und die Fachexpert:innen unserer Kunden, reviewst gegen Suchintention und Zitierfähigkeit und entscheidest, was publiziert wird. Du baust Content-Audits, findest Kannibalisierung und Substanzlücken und leitest daraus einen Redaktionsplan ab, der auch in sechs Monaten noch trägt. Die Texte schreiben andere. Die Richtung gibst du.
  • AI Visibility aufbauen: Du arbeitest an konsistenter Entitätsdarstellung (strukturierte Daten, sameAs, Wikidata, Branchenverzeichnisse), an zitierfähigen Inhalten und an Präsenz in den Quellen, aus denen LLMs tatsächlich zitieren.
  • AI Visibility messbar machen: Prompt-Set-basierter Share of Voice über ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Copilot und Google AI Mode – inklusive Auswertung von GPTBot-, OAI-SearchBot- und PerplexityBot-Zugriffen in den Logfiles.   • Verantwortung im Retainer: Du steuerst mehrere Kundenaccounts parallel, arbeitest in vereinbarten Stundenbudgets, führst die monatlichen Reporting-Calls und Quarterly Reviews und flaggst Scope-Themen früh statt spät.

description:
Short description

Join Septeo CNEE and support challenging client projects in the insolvency industry from the initial requirements gathering through to successful implementation. You’ll combine technical expertise with consulting skills to develop customized solutions for complex business processes. Rather than working on a standard product or processing tickets, you’ll collaborate with our clients to design customized workflows, migrations, and integrations that deliver direct, practical value.

If you enjoy taking on responsibility, contributing to technical development, and interacting with clients, we look forward to receiving your application.

This role is available throughout Germany. Since interacting with clients and the team is a key part of the position, we expect you to be present at our Karlsruhe office on a regular basis and to attend occasional on-site client meetings.


Your mission

  • Design and development of custom extensions, interfaces, workflows, and integrations based on C#/.NET, VBA, and XML
  • Further development and maintenance of an Access-based business application and the underlying MS SQL Server database structures
  • Integration and development of digital case management solutions (eIP, e2A), the Electronic Court and Administrative Mailbox (EGVP), and the integration of electronic signatures
  • Development of pragmatic and sustainable solutions for complex business and technical requirements
  • Consulting and technical support for clients in the digitization and optimization of business processes in the insolvency sector
  • Technical coordination with clients and collaboration with specialized departments within the judiciary
  • Preparation of technical documentation and ensuring proper version control using Git


Your profile

  • Several years of work experience in software development or technical consulting in a project-oriented environment
  • In-depth knowledge of C#/.NET, MS Access, MS SQL Server, VBA, and ideally modern web technologies such as Angular, React, or Blazor
  • Experience in analyzing business requirements as well as designing, implementing, and deploying custom software solutions, integrations, and migrations
  • Experience working with electronic signatures and, ideally, electronic legal transactions (e.g., EGVP) or comparable regulated environments
  • A strong understanding of business processes, as well as a passion for providing technical consulting and collaborating with clients
  • A structured, independent, and solution-oriented approach to work, combined with strong communication and teamwork skills
  • Excellent English and German language skills


Application process

Digital Get-to-Know-You Session 
During a brief conversation with our recruiters, we’ll discuss our mutual expectations.
Technical Interview
Next, you’ll get to know the department and gain deeper insights into our projects, technologies, and way of working.
Introduction day in Karlsruhe
Finally, you’ll visit our headquarters in Karlsruhe. You’ll meet the team, gain insights into real client projects, and get an authentic sense of how we collaborate and work.


Benefits

Our full range of benefits and perks is explained as part of our recruiting process, but you can already get a good overview on our careers page: https://www.stp.one/en/careers
As a European company, our benefits vary by country, but some benefits apply to all employees:

  • Annual training budget and defined career paths
  • Employee referral bonus
  • Mobility: e.g., bike leasing, public transportation subsidies
  • Workation: up to 30 days per year within the EU
  • Screen work glasses
  • Tax-free benefits
  • Events & company parties (summer party, annual kick-off, etc.)
  • Flexible work models (hybrid, remote work, part-time, etc.)
  • English courses for all levels


Contact details

If you have any questions, please feel free to contact our recruiter!

Isabel Ostwald

description:
Your new team:

Would you like to build Salesforce solutions that directly improve the experience of thousands of customers? At auxmoney, you will join a dynamic, cross functional team with a strong focus on customer satisfaction and a 360 degree view of the customer journey. You will work at the intersection of tech, product, and business, shaping scalable platform capabilities and reliable workflows that support one of Europe’s leading fintech platforms.


What you can expect:

  • Own end to end delivery: You architect, implement, and maintain high quality Salesforce solutions across Apex, Flows, LWC, and data models, and you take technical ownership from design to release.
  • Build strong architectures: You apply clean architecture, testability, and performance best practices, and you raise the bar for maintainable code across the platform.
  • Deliver great Salesforce UX: You design and optimize Lightning Web Components with strong performance, thoughtful interaction patterns, and a focus on usable, scalable experiences.
  • Secure by design: You implement robust security and sharing concepts aligned with Salesforce’s security model, including profiles, permission sets, role hierarchy, sharing rules, and field level security.
  • Integrate with confidence: You design and implement integrations via REST and SOAP, platform events, and connectors with resilient patterns, strong authentication, and thorough error handling.
  • Optimize for scale: You build within Salesforce governor limits and enforce best practices for bulkification, caching, transaction management, and async processing.
  • Raise engineering standards: You define and champion platform standards, coding conventions, code reviews, and design guidelines as a trusted technical authority.
  • Mentor and multiply impact: You coach junior and mid level developers through pair programming, structured knowledge sharing, and pragmatic guidance that improves team output.
  • Partner across stakeholders: You collaborate closely with Product, Data, and Operations to translate complex business needs into scalable technical designs and delivery plans.
  • Test for trust: You set expectations for meaningful unit and integration testing, and you help the team maintain strong, reliable coverage that supports safe delivery.
  • Keep the platform reliable: You strengthen observability and maintainability through documentation, architectural decision records, and practical knowledge sharing.
  • Work setup: You will work remotely within Germany, with collaboration routines that keep delivery fast, aligned, and transparent.


Your profile

  • Seasoned Salesforce development: You bring extensive hands on Salesforce development experience (8+ years) in enterprise environments and a track record of delivering impact at scale.
  • Technical leadership: You are advanced in Flows and highly proficient in Apex and OOP, and you confidently choose the right approach across Flow, Apex, and configuration.
  • Strong LWC expertise: You have deep experience with Lightning Web Components, including lifecycle, reactivity, performance optimization, and UI and UX best practices.
  • Security and compliance mindset: You understand Salesforce’s security and sharing model and design for least privilege from the start.
  • Integration skills: You connect Salesforce to external systems via REST and SOAP, OAuth, and named or external credentials, and you select suitable integration patterns for complex scenarios.
  • Built for scale: You consistently apply best practices in governor limits, bulkification, transactions, async processing, and error handling, and you help others do the same.
  • Delivery discipline: You work fluently with Git and pull requests, and you have hands on experience with CI and CD for Salesforce, for example Salesforce DX and GitHub Actions.
  • Clear communication: You communicate technical concepts clearly in English and collaborate effectively in cross functional teams.
  • Nice to have: You bring German skills, Salesforce certifications such as PD I or PD II, Architect track progress, and experience with managed packages, platform events, and Data Loader or ETL.


What we offer:

  • Flexibility for Your Lifestyle: Enjoy family-friendly working hours and a generous home office policy, allowing you to stay agile and flexible in any situation.
  • Ergonomic Work Environment: For your office days, we provide ergonomic workstations that offer you a comfortable and healthy workspace.
  • Independent Work: With short decision-making paths, we enable you to work autonomously and actively contribute your ideas – we provide space for you to take on responsibility.
  • Grow with Us: Unlock your potential with numerous opportunities for growth and development, along with an annual development budget to help you achieve your professional and personal goals.
  • Team Spirit: Team spirit is important to us – we regularly host events and parties where fun is guaranteed.
  • Mobility Your Way: Whether you prefer a train ticket or parking – we support your choice of preferred mobility.
  • Stay Active: Keep fit with a discounted membership at Fitness First or Urban Sports Club, or use our in-house fitness room to stay active after work and enhance your work-life balance.
  • Secure Your Future: Think about your future – we offer subsidies for company pension plans so you can plan long-term with us.
  • Tailored Benefits: We consider your personal life situation – whether you're a parent or love to travel, we offer customized benefits to suit your lifestyle.
Your perspective: You will shape how auxmoney builds and scales its Salesforce platform by owning end to end delivery and influencing technical standards. Your work will directly improve reliability, speed, and quality across customer facing and operational processes. You will grow your impact through mentoring and by helping define future architecture decisions.

Our AI receptionist, Luna, answers and automates phone calls and she’s loved by hundreds of medical practitioners. description:
WHO WE ARE

Proxima Fusion is Europe’s fastest-growing fusion company and the continent’s best-funded fusion player, as well as the first spin-out from the Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics (IPP). Backed by over €650M and powered by a growing team across Munich, Zurich, and Oxford, we are developing the hardware and infrastructure needed to deliver the world’s first commercial stellarator fusion power plant.

Our concept advances the most mature fusion technology out there, the Wendelstein 7-X stellarator, through two next-generation machines: Alpha and Stellaris. Our work combines stellarator optimization, advanced computation, machine learning, and high-temperature superconducting magnets to unlock higher-performance designs that were previously out of reach.

Turning these designs into a functioning fusion power plant requires excellence and ownership across every discipline, from physics and engineering to software, manufacturing, law, and business functions.

 

WHY JOIN PROXIMA FUSION

  • Work on a civilisation-scale problem - Clean, baseload fusion energy is one of the few genuinely world-changing challenges, and every hire in Finance, People, or Legal directly accelerates the path to a working stellarator.

  • Grow as fast as the company does - With headcount set to roughly 5x in a few years and major technical milestones ahead on the path to our demo machine and first power plant, your role grows under you; today's hire is tomorrow's function lead.

  • Tackle problems that don't exist elsewhere - Fusion sits at a rare intersection of deep-tech R&D, industrial procurement, government relations, and venture financing, so non-tech functions face challenges no other workplace can offer.

YOUR IMPACT

As a microwave design engineer, you will help build the basis for the millimeter wave hardware acting as the spark plug that initiates a fusion plasma and raises its temperature to greater than 100 million degrees. You’ll join the Alpha Heating System team ready to drive the integrated RF and thermo-mechanical design of high-power components, and help build and test these components in the lab before installing them at scale on our net scientific gain Alpha stellarator.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

  • Provide innovative solutions to complex RF engineering challenges by collaborating closely with physicists to ensure component designs meet the Alpha plasma physics and thermal-mechanical constraints.

  • Develop designs and evaluate vendor designs to determine an optimal path to efficiently deliver our power to the stellarator - driving down the denominator of input power that will limit fusion power plant gain Q=Pout/Pin - and drive down costs.

  • Draw from and contribute to our stellarator development process, interfacing your RF components with other stellarator systems.

  • Contribute to mechanical and thermal analysis and sensitivity studies for component viability under the loads and stresses imposed by the combination of vacuum, magnetic fields, temperatures, and MW-scale RF loads.

  • Interface with the Alpha project management teams to realize the delivery of RF components and meet the tight Proxima timelines.

WHO YOU ARE

  • A highly capable RF engineer with experience in millimeter waves and knowledge of the tools and best practices for design of these systems

  • Demonstrated familiarly with RF modeling codes - SURF3D, CST, COMSOL, GdfidL, openEMS, even self-developed python codes or ones plasma physics community hasn’t heard of - capable of performing modeling at 200 GHz frequencies

  • Experience validating first-of-a-kind designs with uncertain performance, working as part of a team on multi-scale and multi-physics simulations, testing, and prototyping.

  • Exceptional communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to articulate complex technical concepts clearly and persuasively.

  • Experience with gyrotrons and associated components - transmission systems, launcher antennas, rf loads; experience with plasma physics is a plus.

INTERVIEW PROCESS

  • Recruiter Interview (30-60 min)

  • Technical Screening (30 min)

  • Technical Panel (3x60 min)

To get there, we need a high-performing, diverse team that brings different perspectives, challenges assumptions, and builds together with purpose. We know that diversity of thought and experience leads to better ideas, stronger execution, and a more resilient team. We don’t look at how you identify, what you look like, who you choose to worship or what ethnicity you are. We care about what you can bring to the table.

Mapbox is the leading real-time location platform for a new generation of location-aware businesses. Mapbox is the only platform that equips organizations with the full set of tools to power the navigation of people, packages, and vehicles everywhere. More than 4 million registered developers have chosen Mapbox because of the platform’s flexibility, security and privacy compliance. Organizations use Mapbox applications, data, SDKs and APIs to create customized and immersive experiences that delight their customers. 

What you'll do

This role is scoped by skill rather than by product. The problems below span multiple departments and show up across our Search and Places data work, our Location and Navigation Intelligence work, and the Platform work that makes Mapbox usable by agents. You'll be hired into one specific team or product area, but you'll work across teams where your expertise meets the highest-priority AI problems. You should expect to move between teams and tech stacks as the work demands.

At this level you own the technical design and delivery of a multi-component AI system, and you are accountable for the quality of what ships in your area.

In this role, you will:

  • Define how the products you own should work, build a measurement framework for it, and build evaluation systems for non-deterministic behavior. Formulate hypotheses around the products we build and seek the signal needed to validate them. Define what a correct result is for a given input and state, determine whether to assemble datasets from real usage or hand-written cases, and gate changes on regression results.

  • Run continuous evaluation of the products we build, whether APIs, SDKs, data representations, or reference applications, from the position of the end user, whether developer, agent, or consumer. Assess the gaps such as misuse of parameters or integration anti-patterns, recommend the fixes, and make sure they land.

  • Own the MVP against an agreed north star technical design, and balance technical perfection against shipping useful increments.

  • Build data pipelines and the tooling around them: ingestion, conflation, entity resolution, quality checks, and the batch and streaming jobs that keep a large dataset current.

  • Track and pull external datasets, models, and benchmarks from published research and open-source releases. Evaluate what fits the problem and constraints , and decide when to adopt what exists versus build your own.

  • Design feedback loops so that using a product generates data that improves it. Instrument systems so failures arrive with enough context to reproduce, then turn the recurring ones into evaluation cases.

  • Design the boundary between a model and the tools it calls. Build or improve the model harness, decide what the model handles, what it delegates, and how to keep it working from the state it actually fetched.

  • Work to a latency and cost target per request: streaming, partial results, caching, model routing, prompt structure.

  • Build the internal harnesses and tools (CLI, MCP, and others) your team needs to iterate quickly, and share the parts that generalize with other teams.

  • Raise the bar on your team through code and design review, and bring other engineers up on eval practice.

  • Some of the technical questions in this area are still open. You will help answer them.

  • Participate in an on-call rotation to ensure our systems remain available to customers 24/7. Team members alternate as the on-call primary responder, which may require immediate response outside normal working hours, including weekends.

What We Believe are Important Traits for This Role

  • Required Education/Certification:

    • Bachelors Degree in STEM discipline and 5+ years of software engineering experience, with production ownership of services, pipelines, or SDKs.

  • Technical Skills & Tools (Must-Haves):

    • 2+ years shipping LLM-backed features to real users, in systems that carried error budgets, on-call rotations, and customers who noticed regressions.

    • Data engineering depth: SQL, at least one distributed processing framework, and experience with pipelines where a wrong record mattered more than a slow one.

    • Fluency with tool calling and agent orchestration, including the failure modes: stale context, hallucinated arguments, silent partial success, unbounded loops.

    • Strong Python or TypeScript, and comfort reading code in whatever language the caller happens to be written in.

  • Core Competencies & Scope:

    • Direct experience or deep understanding of designing evaluations for non-deterministic systems. You can describe a dataset you built and the failure it caught.

    • Working knowledge of more than one agent harness, and opinions about where each of them is weak.

    • Experience diagnosing latency in a distributed request path.

    • Comfort with ambiguity, and the judgment to ship something narrow that works while the general solution is still unclear.

Nice to Have Traits for this Role

  • Geospatial data experience: routing, geocoding, POI or address data, OpenStreetMap, or conflation of overlapping sources.

  • Public API or SDK design experience, particularly for developers you never talk to.

  • Experience building against MCP or similar tool transports.

  • Experience running evals in CI, with a commercial harness or one you built.

  • Automotive, in-vehicle infotainment, CarPlay, or Android Auto experience.

  • Voice pipeline experience: streaming ASR, TTS, barge-in, endpointing, wake word.

  • Work under constrained compute, offline, or intermittent connectivity.

  • Experience operating a product through its first external integrations, where the customer finds the gaps before you do.

Employment Requirements

  • Employment Type: Full-time

  • Weekly Hours: 40 h per week

  • Location/Hybrid Policy: Remote (from any city in Germany)

What We Value

In addition to our core values, which are not unique to this position and are necessary for Mapbox leaders:

  • We value high-performing creative individuals who dig into problems and opportunities.

  • We believe in individuals being their whole selves at work. We commit to this through supportive health care, parental leave, flexibility for the things that come up in life, and innovating on how we think about supporting our people.

  • We emphasize an environment of teaching and learning to equip employees with the tools needed to be successful in their function and the company.

  • We strongly believe in the value of growing a diverse team and encourage people of all backgrounds, genders, ethnicities, abilities, and sexual orientations to apply.

 

How we support you

  • Hybrid/Remote Options: Enjoy flexibility to work comfortably from home or periodically from an office where applicable.

  • Country-Specific Care & Coverage: Private health, dental, and income protection plans tailored to elevate your regional statutory benefits.

  • Family-First Support: Family care, maternity and paternity leave policies to support your growing family.

  • Lifestyle Spending Account: Contributions to support your health, wellness, and personal growth

  • Balance & Brainpower: Mental health support for you and your dependents.

  • Rest & Recharge: Paid time away, company holidays, and generous absence policies.

  • Time Off to Give Back: Dedicated paid volunteering time in addition to your standard PTO.

We are seeking an experienced Spacecraft Thermal Verification Engineer to join our Thermal Control System team. You will be the technical lead for the preparation, execution and exploitation of thermal verification activities by test across the Nyx program. You will own spacecraft-level thermal test campaigns, including Thermal Vacuum (TVAC) and Thermal Balance testing, support AIT with the Thermal Control System Flight Model integration and verification, coordinate thermal qualification activities with other sub-systems, and ensure compliance with spacecraft verification requirements.

You will work closely with System Engineering, AIT, Test facilities, Program, Avionics and Propulsion. You will be part of the TCS & ECLSS Team and will report to the Principal Thermal Control System Engineer.

Key Responsibilities

Lead Thermal Vacuum and Thermal Balance Campaigns

  • Define test objectives, verification logic and success criteria of the Nyx system TVAC campaign

  • Develop test plans, test procedures and operational concepts with other functional chains and AIT

  • Prepare and lead Test Readiness Reviews, Test Review Board and NCR Board

  • Lead test logic and execution of spacecraft, subsystem and components thermal test campaigns.

  • Drive anomaly and NCR investigations and technical decision-making during testing.

  • Present campaign status and recommendations to project leadership.

  • Deliver test reports and verification evidence packages

Own Thermal Test Verification Strategy

  • Ensure thermal requirements are properly verified through test, inspection or demonstration.

  • Build and maintain verification events.

  • Drive verification closure toward Qualification Review and Flight Readiness Review.

  • Support Technical Reviews, Design Reviews and Qualification Reviews.

  • Ensure TCS verification activities by tests remain aligned with program priorities, schedules and risks.

Support Flight Model Integration and AIT

  • Work alongside AIT teams during spacecraft assembly and integration.

  • Define thermal instrumentation strategies and test configurations.

  • Support installation, verification and troubleshooting of thermal hardware.

  • Participate in integrated spacecraft functional testing.

  • Support leak testing, functional testing, fluid loop commissioning and system check-outs.

Drive Thermal Test Data Exploitation

  • Support pre-test thermal predictions.

  • Analyze thermal test results.

  • Assess subsystem and spacecraft performance.

  • Identify design improvements and operational recommendations.

  • Ensure lessons learned are captured and disseminated across the organization.

What We Are Looking For

Required Experience

The Localization team builds and owns the systems that make sure every merchant, in every one of our 38 markets, can understand and use our products in their own language. It's one of the most critical enablers of SumUp's global growth, sitting at the heart of how fast and how well we can go to market anywhere in the world.

As our Senior Full Stack Engineer, you'll bring dedicated engineering ownership by working closely with the team to scope, build and ship the systems, integrations and tooling accelerate the ongoing evolution of our localization platform towards greater automation, scalability and end-to-end integration. If you want autonomy, meaningful scope, and the chance to shape a growing function, this is the role.

What you'll do:

  • Design, build and optimise localization solutions across product, CMS, CRM, marketing and design systems, so content moves faster without compromising quality
  • Improve the localization management platform to give the team greater visibility and control while reducing manual steps
  • Embed automated language and quality checks into several steps of the localization workflows, catching issues before they reach production
  • Improve the experience for developers, designers, marketers and content teams by ensuring localization solutions support their processes and ways of working
  • Partner with Web and Mobile, Website, Comms Platform and other technical teams to enable localization capabilities across the technology stack
  • Explore how AI and language technology can strengthen and future-proof the localization stack, while ensuring solutions meet evolving compliance requirements.

You'll be great for this role if:

  • Strong background in backend engineering, ideally with Go (alternatively knowledge with Python, Rust or C++)
  • Experience building and maintaining RESTful APIs in a microservices or distributed systems environment
  • Working knowledge of databases such as PostgreSQL and event streaming tools such as Kafka
  • Comfort translating priorities from non technical stakeholders into scoped, shippable engineering work
  • Ability to operate independently across a fragmented, distributed system landscape, working within architecture owned by other teams
  • Exposure to frontend frameworks such as Reactjs and languages like Typescript
  • Experience working with translation management systems (TMS), or with the localization of web or mobile applications and other content platforms.

Why you should join SumUp

🌎 Opportunity to work with SumUppers globally on large-scale fintech products used by millions of businesses worldwide, from our Berlin office. This involves an office-first setup

💶 A corporate pension scheme where we match up to 20% of your contributions

🏖 Generous time off: enjoy 28 days of paid leave plus public holidays and special leave days

🎁 Numerous other benefits such as Urban Sports Club subsidy, Kita placement assistance, subsidised office lunches

🌴 Break4me: 1-month sabbatical after 3 years of service🔗 Referral Bonus: earn additional rewards by referring talented individuals to join the SumUp team

Be empowered to do more that matters.

At SumUp, we're on a mission to empower small businesses across the globe by providing simple and affordable tools that allow them to thrive. Today, over 4 million businesses in 38 markets rely on SumUp as their financial partner to manage payments, finance and customer relationships.

Compensation: €65k-90k + 25% of your base salary in equity on top
Location: Berlin (Hybrid, 2+ days/week in office); open for candidates willing to relocate to Berlin


About koppla

At koppla, we're a fun and ambitious team on a mission to help the construction industry build more efficiently. We're already partnering with top construction companies and delivering impressive results for our customers (multi-months speed-ups discovered through koppla).

Our ambitions are backed by leading VCs (Earlybird, Newion) and industry angels as we tackle a billion-dollar opportunity problem in an underdigitized and underserved market.

Our culture is core to who we are and we've built one we're genuinely proud of. We are not looking for hypergrowth - we believe in hiring slowly to create an environment of few but very high-performing team members that build a truly great product (similar to Netflix, Ashby or Linear).


What you'll be doing

  • Collaborate closely with product managers, designers and engineers to design and implement new features in a truly cross-functional process.
  • Build and maintain user-facing parts (in Vue) as well as backend services and APIs 
  • Contribute to the overall architecture of the entire system
  • Collaborate with and learn from senior engineers to implement best practices for software development, infrastructure, and deployment processes. Participate in code reviews and provide constructive feedback to peers while learning from more experienced engineers.
Our Tech Stack: 
  • Frontend: Typescript, Vue 3, Tailwind, Netlify, GH Actions 
  • Backend: Typescript, AWS, NestJS, Prisma, PostgreSQL, REST, Websockets, Terraform, GH Actions


Who we're looking for

This role is perfect for a Frontend/Full Stack Engineer with 2-5 years of experience looking to grow their skills and make a meaningful impact at a company that is approaching product-market fit (> €2.5M ARR). You are likely a great fit if:

  • You believe in quality and want to build the best possible experience for our end users - because you care about them.
  • You have solid engineering fundamentals, write clean and efficient code, and are eager to continue elevating your skills.
  • You are focussed on FE, but flexible to switch to BE depending on the task - it could be 50/50 at times but also 80/20 if needed. In the long run you want to become full stack
  • You understand how to balance technical trade-offs and can contribute to discussions about scalability, performance, and maintainability.
  • You thrive in a fast-paced startup environment, enjoy taking ownership of your tasks, and stay proactive and pragmatic in solving challenges.

Beyond the role-specific requirements, you also see your own values reflected in our Culture Playbook.


What we offer

  • A company of co-owners through tax-optimized equity grants.
  • A culture with a focus on transparency, respect, ownership, collaboration and the well-being of each team member on this exciting journey.
  • An environment that values hard-work while still allowing work-life/family integration through 28 days PTO, flexible working hours, workation and a hybrid setup.
  • Dog-friendly with free lunch, besides beverages and snacks as well as a home office budget at start.
  • And more: Annual personal training budget of 1,500€ (FTE), Company supported pension Scheme (”BAV”, 30% contribution), Urban Sports Club Membership, Home Office budget and more.

The role

We’re looking for a Senior Python Engineer, Platform Libraries (m/f/d) to join our team and play a key role in developing software that connects and translates lab equipment hardware interfaces, automates machines, and powers our next-generation automation platform. As a core team member, you will be working on cutting-edge technology, building software that bridges the gap between software and hardware, enabling seamless integration across various vendors.

Connectors are how we do it. Every instrument we bring online gets one, and every connector is built on our shared Python libraries: Bus, our Connector Development Kit, and the stack underneath them.

Our mission is to empower researchers and engineers by bridging the gap between lab equipment and cloud-based automation. Our customers are solving critical challenges like curing diseases, developing sustainable materials, and addressing global food security. We provide them with the tools to connect their devices, automate workflows, and unlock new possibilities in R&D.

Your mandate has two halves. Own the libraries as a product with real users, our own engineers today and external contributors later. And stay close enough to customer connector work that what you build is grounded in problems that actually exist.


Why you'll love this role

Your users are engineers. Your success lets other people ship connectors faster. That's a different craft from shipping features, and it's the one we're hiring for.

Real hardware, real failure modes. Instruments time out, return garbage, and arrive with documentation that's wrong. You'll debug against physical devices in our Munich workshop.


Open source on purpose. Our CDK and our standardization work (SiLA 2) are public. What you build gets used and criticized by people outside the company.


Senior scope, small team. You'll be the person who decides how connector engineering works here. No layer between you and that decision.


Your mission

1. The Builder: own the shared libraries

  • Own Bus, the CDK, and the core stack. Features, tests, CI, releases, and deprecations across the connectors already running in production.

  • Extract abstractions from real work. When the same pattern shows up in the third connector, it becomes a library feature. You're the one who notices, and the one who does it.

  • Make the docs good enough to remove yourself. An outside contributor should be able to build a connector on our libraries without a call.

  • Set the quality standard. You define what "tested" means before a connector reaches a customer, and you make it stick.

2. The Shipper: build connectors on real instruments

  • Ship production connectors end to end. Spec sheet, physical device, protocol, proof of connectivity, tested connector, live customer. Independently.

  • Reverse-engineer what isn't documented. Roughly half the instruments we touch have incomplete or wrong docs. Packet captures, trial and error, vendor calls.

  • Work with the workshop. Our Connector Factory team gets instruments development-ready. You take it from there.

  • Talk to the people who use it. Automation engineers and scientists at biotech and pharma customers. Their constraints shape what the libraries need next.


Your profile

  • Deep Python: 5+ years of writing production Python other people depend on. Async, typing, packaging, testing. You've designed APIs that other engineers built on, not just glue code.

  • You've debugged a real protocol against real hardware: gRPC, serial, TCP, OPC UA, CAN, USB. Which one matters less than having sat with a packet capture and a device that won't respond.

  • You ship without a spec: When the documentation is wrong, you reverse-engineer, instead of filing a vendor ticket and waiting. 

  • You build for other developers: An SDK, a library, an internal platform. Something where your job was making other engineers faster.

  • Located in Munich: The instruments are physically here at WERK1. 


Nice to have

  • SiLA 2, or another device abstraction and interoperability standard

  • Lab automation, scientific instruments, or a life science background

  • Open source maintainership with actual external contributors

  • C, C++, .NET, or Rust, for the vendor DLLs and drivers we end up wrapping

  • Docker, Kubernetes, edge deployment

  • German, for vendor conversations


Probably not a fit if

Better to say this now than in week 6.


  • Your Python is all APIs and databases and you've never debugged a physical device.

  • You'd want two quarters to redesign the library architecture before shipping a connector.

  • You like shipping integrations but have no appetite for going back afterwards to generalise, test, and document.

  • You want the library work without the customer deadlines. Both are in the job.

UniteLabs is on the mission to accelerate scientific progress by automating lab processes with scalable infrastructure.

The best developers don't wait for a customer to tell them something's broken.

They catch it first, in the pull request, in staging, or in the checkout flow at 3am, before a single user notices. That instinct is Checkly's whole reason to exist. We give developers and their agents the tools to own reliability the way they own their code: end-to-end tests and synthetic monitoring defined as code, powered by OpenTelemetry and Playwright, versioned and reviewed like everything else they ship. From pull request to post-mortem, in one place.

Thousands of them, from modern AI companies like Mistral and resolve.ai to large engineering orgs like LinkedIn, Citi, and 1Password, build with us. In 2024 we raised $20M in Series B funding from Balderton, CRV and Accel.

Here's the thing about 2026: AI agents and coding assistants are shipping more software, faster, than any team could review by hand, and more of it is breaking in ways nobody has seen before. LLM-backed features fail probabilistically. Agents take actions no runbook anticipated. "Is my app healthy?" is becoming an unanswerable question for a whole generation of AI-native software. You will build reliability for this kind of software.

Our stack is AI (Codex, Claude, use what you like best), Vue.js, TypeScript, Node.js, Golang, Postgres, ClickHouse and AWS. We ship to prod all day, every day. We practice Agile (not scrum) and take pride in good documentation and good looking products.

We’re a remote-first startup that keeps things simple—low on meetings, high on productivity, and always shipping. If you love building cool things, working async, actually listening to and working with customers, and keeping it lean, you’ll fit right in!

What you'll do

Build and ship with AI

You will actively use coding agents for full stack development, from exploring solutions and generating scaffolding to refactoring, test generation and debugging. At Checkly we push the limits of AI tools every day.

Talk to our users

You will talk directly to the developers, DevOps and Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) teams who are on-call, debugging incidents, or wiring Checkly into production pipelines. You will understand their workflows, pain points, and feedback. You use those conversations to validate ideas, course-correct early, and iterate on what you build. Customer calls and the weekly support rotation are part of the job, not a distraction from it.

Find the right problems to solve

In a world where the cost of building software trends to zero, the hard part is picking what to build. You will focus on real developer pain: flaky tests and flaky checks, unclear failures, noisy alerts. You will favour pragmatic solutions that ship quickly, validate assumptions in production, and compound into long-term reliability improvements.

Own your work end to end

From shaping the initial idea, through implementation and rollout, to watching how it behaves in production. You will take part in on-call and help support customers when things don’t work as expected.

What you should have

  • You have shipped features with AI, not just experimented with them. You have taken work from zero to shipped with a comparable stack, made implementation decisions that held up, and put things in front of real users.

  • You have built and run production software. You know the realities of operating software that people depend on: edge cases, incidents, regressions, and the need for observability and follow-up. You are not surprised when things break. You help fix them.

  • You can hold a product conversation, not just a technical one. You can look at a customer problem and reason about whether the thing we are about to build actually solves it.

  • You work well without an office around you. You are autonomous and self-motivated in a remote setup, and you still enjoy getting to know your colleagues and helping other people get unstuck.

  • FULLY remote role, within the UTC-3 to UTC+3 time zones. You need to be able to travel to (other) European countries without having to wait for a visa appointment, for our annual kickoff, a team meetup or a conference.

What you will hate about us

We would rather tell you now than have you find out in month two.

  • We use AI for everything, and we mean everything. AI skepticism is not a thing here. If you have the slightest hesitation about working with AI every day, this is not the place for you, and that is completely fine.

  • We write more than we talk. We are async-first, so a lot of decisions happen in documents and threads, not meetings. If you do your best thinking out loud in a room full of people, you will miss it here.

  • We are lean, so you own the unglamorous parts too. There is no separate QA team, no ops layer to hand things off to, and you are on the support rotation and the on-call rotation like everyone else.

  • We ship constantly and change our minds. Priorities move as we learn from customers. If you need long, stable planning cycles, this will feel chaotic.

  • Customer signals come first, and most of the time they matter more than your instinct. We build what customers actually want, not the clever thing we dreamed up.

  • Remote-first, flexible work hours, async-first (low meeting, high productivity) and transparent culture

Welcome to Miaplaza!

Our vision is to elevate online learning by applying the most successful approaches in virtual education to create an accessible and inclusive homeschool curriculum platform where all students can be successful! Our K-8 platforms include Miacademy, Always Icecream, and Clever Dragons, and our 9-12 options include MiaPrep and MiaPrep Online High School. Our student base is rapidly growing, and we’re hiring for multiple positions across several departments! Our expansion stems from our commitment to providing exceptional educational content and our pursuit of new opportunities. 🚀

▶️ You can hear our CEO, Johannes Ziegler, discuss our company’s values and future!

How you’ll make an impact (position summary):

Miaplaza is dedicated to making education engaging and accessible through innovative online learning platforms. We develop personalized learning experiences for students, helping them grow in a supportive and interactive environment. Our vision is to elevate online learning by applying the most successful approaches in virtual education to create an accessible and inclusive education curriculum platform where all students can be successful!

The Role

We're looking for a QA Engineer to join our current QA team. You'll take ownership of how we test, validate, and sign off on quality across our platform. We're actively investing in our QA practice: expanding automated test coverage, improving our release testing process, and moving toward a model where quality is embedded throughout the development lifecycle.

You'll report to a technical Engineering Manager and work alongside engineers who value clear test documentation, reliable automation, and confident code releases.

As a mature company, we have legacy systems and established manual testing workflows, but we are transitioning to modern automated testing practices using Playwright and TypeScript. The split between manual and automated work varies, but you should be comfortable working across both, bringing automation where it adds the most value while pragmatically maintaining manual coverage where it's still the right tool.

A core goal of our QA evolution is to make testing faster, more reliable, and less dependent on last-minute changes before each release: replacing fragile manual regression cycles with stable automated suites, reducing flakiness, and building coverage that the whole team can rely on. Every testing investment is measured by whether it improves quality and reduces the team's burden at release time.

What You'll Do

  • Write and maintain automated regression tests; review automation MRs from peers

  • Execute manual testing across web UIs (functional, regression, cross-platform, responsive layouts on mobile/tablet)

  • Create and maintain test cases, checklists, and test documentation in TestRail

  • File clear, actionable bug reports with reproduction steps; collaborate with developers to triage and resolve

  • Own the release testing process to ensure only high-quality changes ship

  • Partner with PMs and designers on requirements review, edge cases, and acceptance criteria

  • Contribute to QA process improvements as we scale (currently a 2-person team growing to 4)

How We Work

We believe you should know what your days look like before you accept an offer.

We don't have much bureaucracy. Small team, direct communication, short decision loops. If you've worked at places where opening a Jira ticket to request a Jira ticket was normal, this isn't that. Here's the reality:

Meetings (yes, we keep them minimal):

  • Daily standup with your product team. Show up, share updates and unblock each other..

  • Sprint planning and retrospectives with your product team, once per sprint.

  • 1:1 with your Engineering Manager - Regular cadence, your agenda.

  • Monthly Engineering all-hands.

  • That's it. The rest of your time is yours to work.

Deployments:

  • Bi-monthly release cadence with a schedule published in advance. As a QA Engineer, you own the release testing window. Coordinating with developers, running regression suites, and signing off on quality before the release.

  • Infrequent ad-hoc hotfixes

Communication:

  • Async-friendly. Documentation-first.

  • Slack/ Jira/ GitLab MRs/ Notion

  • Google Workspace for email and documents.

  • Zoom for video calls.

Timezone:

  • We need significant overlap with typical CET (Central European Time) working hours to coordinate and collaborate synchronously. Additionally we have stakeholders and developers in US timezones that we occasionally need to meet.


What We're Looking For

Requirements (Requisite Skills): 

  • 2+ years of QA engineering experience, including web UI testing

  • 2+ years of experience with Playwright or a similar test automation framework (e.g. Cypress, Selenium, Puppeteer)

  • 2+ years of experience using TypeScript

  • Strong test design skills: comfortable writing and maintaining test cases, checklists, and test documentation

  • Familiarity with QA's role in the SDLC and how to collaborate with developers and PMs

  • Strong analytical skills and attention to detail

  • Upper-intermediate English (B2+) for written and spoken communication

  • Strong experience in manual testing and writing manual test cases

Nice to have:

  • Experience with accessibility and/or security testing

How you’ll work with other teams:

Career Growth

We have a defined career ladder. Whether your path leads toward Senior/Staff QA Engineer or Engineering Management, there's room to grow - and we'll work with you to get there.

Onboarding

Every team member gets full support throughout onboarding, and no one expects you to figure out the ins and outs on your own. We'll pair with you, answer every question, and make sure you have the context you need. New hires typically feel very supported at Miaplaza.

What success looks like here: In the first couple of months, you're asking a lot of clarifying questions, reading documentation, exploring the product independently, and writing and running tests with confidence. By months 3-4, you're taking ownership of a specific area, building out test coverage, identifying gaps, and driving quality improvements. By month 5-6, you're contributing meaningfully to the testing strategy for migration and modernisation work and operating independently. The common thread: curiosity, initiative, and the habit of investigating before you ask, but always asking when you need to.

Interview Process

Our process is staged and designed to respect your time. Expect a mix of introductory conversation, technical discussion, and practical evaluation. We want to understand how you think about real problems and testing practices. As part of the process, we will ask for professional references and conduct a background check in accordance with applicable law. If you need any accommodations during the interview process, let us know, we're happy to help.

Compensation

Competitive compensation, open to negotiation based on your experience and expertise. We'll discuss specifics early in the process so neither side wastes time. Since we’re remote-first, every arrangement is different; we tailor time off, benefits, and perks as part of your individual contract to ensure the overall package works for both sides.

Ready to apply?

Join our team at Miaplaza! Start by submitting your application and resume. Our hiring process involves a screening call, followed by a behavioral interview, and two technical interviews.

Nice-to-have
  • Erfahrung mit SUSE Stack oder vergleichbaren Kubernetes-Management-Plattformen
  • Kenntnisse in DevSecOps, Policy as Code oder Hochverfügbarkeitskonzepten
  • Erfahrung mit Monitoring-Stacks (z. B. Prometheus, Grafana)
Persönlich
  • Systemisches Denken statt Ticket-Fokus, mit Blick fürs Gesamtbild
  • Sicheres Auftreten und Kommunikation auf Augenhöhe mit Entwicklungsteams wie mit Kunden
  • Strukturierte, eigenständige und lösungsorientierte Arbeitsweise
  • Erfahrung darin, Themen über Team- und Kundengrenzen hinweg zu steuern


Was wir dir bieten

title: Cloud Platform Engineer (m/w/d)

description:
Warum LPE Immobilien?

  • Die Hausverwaltung ist der unterschätzteste Beruf Deutschlands: Kein anderer entscheidet so unmittelbar darüber, wie Menschen wohnen. Trotzdem gilt der Hausverwalter bis heute als Buchhalter mit Schlüsselbund. Wir wollen das ändern, und Software ist dafür einer unserer zentralen Hebel.
  • Mit lpeOS bauen wir die Systeme, mit denen wir selbst jeden Tag arbeiten: das Kundenportal für unsere Eigentümer, KI-Agenten, die eigenständig Aufgaben übernehmen, und das Verwaltercockpit als Arbeitsumgebung unserer Verwalter. Wir digitalisieren unsere eigenen Prozesse, um die Arbeit unserer Verwalter jeden Tag ein Stück besser zu machen, mit dem Anspruch, die Branche zu revolutionieren.
  • Kaum eine Branche wurde von moderner Software so lange übersehen. Der Abstand zwischen dem, was ist, und dem, was möglich ist, ist riesig, und wir bauen ihn Stück für Stück zu. Du wärst eine der ersten Personen im Produktteam.


Was dich bei uns erwartet – Deine Aufgaben

  • Du entwickelst Fullstack in TypeScript, vom Kundenportal über das Verwaltercockpit bis zu den Services und der Infrastruktur dahinter, auf der grünen Wiese und ohne Altlasten. Features verantwortest du end-to-end: von der Idee über die Gestaltung bis zum Release, bei Bedarf auch ohne Designer an deiner Seite.
  • Du baust KI-Agenten als Produktfunktionalität für unsere Verwalter und Kunden. Zugleich entwickeln wir unsere eigene Entwicklungsumgebung permanent weiter: ein modernes Setup rund um Cursor und Claude Code, inklusive Agent-Graph-Loops und Harness.
  • Dabei arbeitest du nah an den Nutzern: Deine Kolleginnen, Kollegen und Kunden sind direkt erreichbar, Feedback bekommst du auf kurzem und direktem Weg. Wir sammeln Probleme, bewerten sie und bauen die wichtigsten in festen Cycles.
  • Unser Stack: TypeScript durchgehend, mit React und Next.js im Frontend und Node im Backend, als Monorepo auf Google Cloud (Infrastructure as Code), dazu Postgres und event-getriebene Prozesse. Du musst nicht alles davon kennen, den Rest lernst du bei uns.


Was du mitbringen solltest

  • 2 bis 4 Jahre Erfahrung in der Webentwicklung.
  • Sichere Praxis in TypeScript oder JavaScript, idealerweise mit React oder Next.js.
  • Ein aktuelles Projekt, das du zeigen kannst: Produktionscode, Side Project oder Open Source.
  • Du arbeitest gern quer über den ganzen Stack und magst Frontend und Backend ähnlich gern.
  • Du verantwortest Features end-to-end und kannst bei Bedarf auch ohne Designer ein gutes Interface gestalten.
  • KI-Tooling ist Teil deines Arbeitsalltags, und du prüfst die Ergebnisse genauso kritisch, wie du sie nutzt.
  • Grundverständnis von Datenbanken (SQL) und API-Design.
  • Du willst verstehen, warum etwas gebaut wird, bevor du es baust.
  • Deutschkenntnisse mindestens auf B2-Niveau.
Du erfüllst nicht alle Punkte? Bewirb dich trotzdem. Talent und Lernkurve zählen bei uns mehr als Jahreszahlen im Lebenslauf.


Was wir dir bieten

  • Eine seltene Ausgangslage. Wir bauen Software für ein Geschäftsmodell, das bereits funktioniert, und wissen, dass sie gebraucht wird. Du erlebst aus nächster Nähe, wie sich eine ganze Branche neu erfindet, und gestaltest das aktiv mit.
  • Echter Impact. Alles, was du baust, kommt bei unseren Verwaltern, Eigentümern und Kunden direkt zum Einsatz.
  • Eine Branche von innen kennenlernen. Die Immobilienwirtschaft ist einer der größten Märkte Deutschlands und steht erst am Anfang ihrer Digitalisierung. Du lernst sie dort kennen, wo die Entscheidungen fallen.
  • Direkte Zusammenarbeit mit den Produktverantwortlichen. Kurze Wege, schnelle Entscheidungen und jemand, der sich Zeit für deine Fragen nimmt.
  • Mentoring und Weiterentwicklung. Wohin du dich entwickeln willst, besprechen wir offen und regelmäßig. Mentoring ist bei uns in alle Richtungen möglich, fachlich wie persönlich.
  • Ehrliches Feedback. Sofort und in beide Richtungen.
  • Die richtigen Werkzeuge. Premium-Hardware, cloudbasierte Tools, aktuelles KI-Tooling, papierlos. Wenn dir etwas fehlt, um besser zu arbeiten, bekommst du es.
  • Perspektive. Diese Stelle ist so gebaut, dass sie mit dir und mit lpeOS wächst.

As our Senior Product Manager, you will play a key role in driving ProGlove's software and solution offering.  
You will operate as the “CEO” of the software and service business inside the company, with accountability for strategy, P&L, growth, customer outcomes, and long-term value creation. The role reports directly to the CPO and will be part of the product management team. 


Your profile

  • Commercially obsessed and outcome-driven
  • You think in terms of value, outcomes, and usage-not features
  • You are comfortable working in dynamic and evolving environments
  • You can navigate both technical and commercial discussions
  • You are curious, pragmatic, and impact-driven
  • You have strong business acumen 
  • You are motivated by building something that changes how a company operates
  • Able to balance short-term performance with long-term value creation
 
 
Core accountabilities

  • ARR growth
  • Attach rate
  • Net Revenue Retention
  • Customer adoption and value realization
  • Pricing and monetization strategy
  • Strategic partnerships
 
Required qualifications 
  • 5to8+ years of experience in product management, preferably in software, cloud, SaaS, or IoT environments
  • Proven experience delivering cloud-based or SaaS products
  • Strong understanding of cloud platforms (e.g., AWS, Azure, GCP)
  • Ability to translate customer needs into scalable product solutions
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making skills
  • Excellent stakeholder management, communication, and facilitation skills, with the ability to influence teams and senior leadership.
  • Professional fluency in English.
Nice to have 
  • Experience in industrial technology, IoT, hardware, embedded systems

  • Background in enterprise or B2B software

  • Experience with product-led growth, monetization


Why us?

At ProGlove, we're building technology that empowers frontline workers to work smarter, faster, and safer. As a Senior Product Manager, you'll be a key pillar in defining the future products and solutions and making them commercially successful. 
What you can expect: 

  • A highly autonomous role with ownership of strategic, cross-functional initiatives.
  • The opportunity to influenceProGlove'sbusiness models.
  • Hybrid working model with regular collaboration with our Munich headquarters.
  • Flexible working hours and modern equipment.
  • Learning and development opportunities, including dedicated learning time and our School of Glove academy.

Strategy & Vision

  • Establish a category-leading position in operational intelligence and frontline analytics

Commercial Growth

Leadership

Customer Outcomes

Our team is focused on bringing new innovations that are appreciated by our customers and to continuously strengthen ProGloves portfolio. We work collaboratively across the entire company and value chain. Together we are not about growing products only; it is about changing how the company grows.

title: Senior Product Manager - Software Solutions

description:
Your mission

As our Product Manager – Android Integration & Ecosystem, you will define the product what and why for how ProGlove devices connect, integrate and create value within the enterprise Android ecosystem.

ProGlove is evolving from a wearable scanner company into a Worker Companion company, bringing together ergonomic wearable hardware, software, connectivity, workflow guidance, data and intelligence. With the MAI Wearable Companion, we are entering a broader ecosystem of enterprise applications, technologies, standards, partners and customer infrastructure.

Your mission will be to make our products easy to adopt, integrate and deploy at scale – without turning every customer opportunity into a bespoke engineering project. You will identify recurring customer needs, translate them into scalable capabilities and propositions, and decide where ProGlove should own, enable or partner. In doing so, you will help turn integration from a technical necessity into a source of differentiation, customer value and commercial opportunity.

You will work closely with the Product Manager responsible for the Wearable Companion device. While they own the device proposition, you will own how the device connects to and creates value in the wider ecosystem. Together, you will shape a coherent end-to-end proposition for customers, developers, integrators and partners.

Your day-to-day 
  • Define and evolve the product strategy and priorities for ProGlove’s enterprise Android integration and ecosystem capabilities, aligned with customer needs and business goals.
  • Work directly with customers, Sales and Solution Architecture to identify recurring problems, distinguish individual requests from broader market needs and turn the right opportunities into scalable solutions.
  • Translate recurring integration needs into repeatable product capabilities such as APIs, SDKs, tools, interfaces, documentation, integration patterns and deployment solutions.
  • Shape the product experience around device setup, provisioning, application distribution, device management and other capabilities required to deploy and operate connected device fleets at scale.
  • Make clear, pragmatic decisions about where ProGlove should own, enable or partner, balancing customer value, strategic control, speed, scalability and technical complexity.
  • Identify the platforms, applications, standards and ecosystem players that matter to our customers, and shape the integrations, certifications and technology partnerships that strengthen our proposition.
  • Explore where integration capabilities, software, services and ecosystem propositions can create differentiated value and support commercial or recurring-revenue opportunities.
  • Partner closely with Engineering and the Product Manager for the Wearable Companion to create alignment on customer problems, priorities, trade-offs and desired outcomes.
  • Enable Sales and other customer-facing teams to clearly explain our Android proposition, supported capabilities, integrations and common deployment patterns.
  • Maintain a forward-looking view of enterprise Android, AOSP, enterprise mobility, AI and adjacent technologies, and translate relevant developments into strategic options and product priorities.


Your profile

At ProGlove, technical expertise matters, but how you work is just as important. We are looking for someone who takes ownership, stays curious, collaborates openly and turns complexity into clear, pragmatic decisions.

  • You bring strong Product Management experience in B2B or enterprise technology and can define strategy, discover meaningful customer problems, prioritize opportunities and turn them into scalable products or propositions.
  • You are commercially minded and naturally connect product decisions with customer value, differentiation, business impact and opportunities to capture value.
  • You are comfortable working with enterprise software, platforms, connected devices, integrations or technology ecosystems, and understand the realities of complex customer IT environments.
  • You have enough technical depth to understand architecture, interfaces and trade-offs, contribute credibly to platform and integration discussions, and recognize when deeper engineering expertise is needed.
  • You think in systems and patterns: when faced with a customer requirement, you look beyond the immediate request to understand why it exists, how broadly it applies and what a simple, repeatable solution could look like.
  • You take end-to-end ownership, move topics forward without waiting for perfect instructions and remain effective when the product space or path ahead is not yet fully defined.
  • You collaborate generously and build trust across Product, Engineering, Sales, Solution Architecture, customers and external partners. You can create alignment and drive decisions without relying on formal authority.
  • You communicate clearly and transparently, raise risks early and can make complex technical and commercial topics understandable to different audiences.
  • You are curious about customers, the business and emerging technologies, and continuously test assumptions rather than pursuing technology for its own sake.
  • You use pragmatic judgment to balance speed, simplicity, quality and long-term value.
  • You are fluent in English and comfortable working in an international environment.

Experience in one or more of the following areas would be valuable, but is not required:

  • Enterprise Android, AOSP or adjacent Android ecosystems, including environments operating outside standard Google Mobile Services.
  • Enterprise mobility management, MDM/EMM, device provisioning, application deployment or connected fleet management.
  • Rugged or industrial devices, IoT or edge devices, connected hardware or other B2B technology ecosystems.
  • APIs, SDKs, developer or integrator experiences and enterprise integrations.
  • Platform or ecosystem strategy, technology partnerships, certification programs or developer and partner ecosystems.
  • Enterprise customers deploying technology at scale.
Direct Android Product Management experience is an advantage, but not essential if you bring strong Product Management expertise and relevant experience from an adjacent enterprise technology ecosystem.


Why us?

This is an opportunity to shape an important part of a category that is still being defined. 
Android gives ProGlove access to a much broader technology ecosystem, but the opportunity goes far beyond compatibility. You will help determine what role ProGlove should play in that ecosystem, which capabilities we should own, where we should partner, what customers and developers should be able to build around us, and where integration itself can become a source of differentiation and recurring business value. 
ProGlove already has the customer base, market credibility, technology and industrial expertise to build on. Our products are used in some of the world's most demanding operational environments. What we are now building is the next layer. 
Over time, success will mean more than making our own products easier to integrate. It will mean creating capabilities, interfaces and ecosystem relationships that customers, application providers and partners actively choose to build around - moving ProGlove from ecosystem participant toward ecosystem shaper. 
If you are excited by the idea of turning complex technology ecosystems into simple, valuable products - and helping shape how the next generation of frontline technology connects with the digital world - we would love to meet you. 
Join us in building the future of frontline work.


What success looks like

  • ProGlove has a clear, customer-backed strategy and prioritized roadmap for Android integration and ecosystem capabilities.
  • Recurring customer and integration needs are turned into scalable, repeatable solutions rather than one-off engineering projects.
  • Customers can adopt, integrate, deploy and manage ProGlove devices more easily within their existing enterprise environments.
  • Decisions about what ProGlove should own, enable or partner are made transparently and based on customer value, business impact and long-term scalability.
  • Product, Engineering, Sales and Solution Architecture are aligned on priorities, supported capabilities and key trade-offs.
  • Customer-facing teams can confidently communicate our Android proposition and common deployment patterns without relying on Product or Engineering in every opportunity.

description:
Deine Mission

syte benutzt komplexe Algorithmen, die auf Basis von 3D-Punktwolken und 3D-Modellen Gebäudemetriken ausrechnen. Typische Beispiele für relevante Metriken sind Geschossfläche, Anzahl Geschosse, Volumen und Gebäudehöhen. Um schnelle Entwicklungszyklen zu gewährleisten, und Änderungen an den Algorithmen auf Knopfdruck quantitativ und automatisiert bewerten zu können, ist syte auf hochwertige QA-Daten angewiesen. Um diesen Datensatz systematisch auszubauen und zu härten und damit die Grundlage, auf der unsere Algorithmen gemessen werden, zu entwickeln, suchen wir dich als Werkstudent Data QA & Algorithm Benchmarking (m/w/d) zum nächstmöglichen Zeitpunkt in Münster. 

Deine Aufgaben

  • Ground Truth Audit: Du evaluierst die Korrektheit bestehender Testdaten und ermittelst hierfür neue Metriken, die wir zur Evaluation unserer Algorithmen verwenden können.
  • Edge Cases jagen: Du ermittelst neue Testdaten für schwierige Gebäude (z.B. komplexe Dachformen, Bäume über den Dächern) und integrierst diese in den Gesamtdatensatz.
  • Data Sourcing: Du ermittelst potenzielle Quellen für neue Testdatensätze und integrierst diese möglichst automatisiert.
  • Benchmarking & Insights: Du führst unsere Benchmarking-Pipelines aus, um sowohl die Algorithmen als auch die Qualität der Daten quantitativ zu bewerten. Die Ergebnisse dieser Analysen visualisierst und kommunizierst du verständlich, sodass sich daraus Handlungsempfehlungen ableiten.
  • Pipeline Engineering: Du implementierst und testest Verbesserungen in den Benchmarking-Pipelines und den Parametern der Algorithmen.


Dein Profil

  • Dein Studium: Du studierst in einem höheren Bachelorsemester oder ersten Mastersemester (Geo-/Wirtschafts-)Informatik oder hast einen Schwerpunkt in Data Science/Statistik. Du hast auch einen gültigen Immatrikulationsnachweis. 
  • Analytische Fähigkeiten: Du arbeitest dich gerne tief in Daten ein und begeisterst dich für die statistische Analyse der Daten.
  • Neugierde für die komplexe Daten: Dir gefällt die Arbeit an und das Nachvollziehen von komplexeren Algorithmen in einer anspruchsvollen Domäne.
  • Teamfähigkeit: Du arbeitest mit hohem Qualitätsanspruch und kannst dich gut im Team koordinieren.
  • Sprachkenntnisse: Du sprichst verhandlungssicheres Deutsch (mind. C1) und fließend Englisch (mind. B2).
  • Pluspunkt: Du hast Vorerfahrungen in den Bereichen Architektur oder PropTech und erste Programmiererfahrungen mit Python.


Dein Einstiegstermin und Einsatzort

  • Einstiegstermin: zum nächstmöglichen Zeitpunkt
  • Einsatzort: Münster (ca. 1 Tag pro Woche im Office)
  • Anstellungsart: Werkstudium (12-20 Std./Woche, Zeiten flexibel)


Deine Benefits

  • Dein attraktives Gehalt: Wir sorgen dafür, dass jeder Aspekt deiner Reise bei syte motivierend ist. Wir kennen deinen Wert!

  • Deine Hardware: Unser syte-Team ist mit modernster Hard- und Software ausgestattet.

  • Dein Team: Einmal im Quartal trifft sich das gesamte Team für zwei Tage zum Arbeiten und um gemeinsam Erfolge zu feiern.

  • Deine Flexibilität: Neben gemeinsamen Workations hast du auch privat die Möglichkeit, aus dem Ausland zu arbeiten.

  • Dein Hund im Büro: Dein vierbeiniger Begleiter ist bei uns herzlich willkommen und darf jederzeit mit dir ins Office kommen.

  • Dein persönliches Benefit-Budget: 2.200,00 € jährlich für das, was dir wichtig ist:

    • Upskilling: Dir steht jeweils ein Budget für betriebliche als auch für private Weiterbildung zur Verfügung.

    • Steueroptimierte Benefits: Du kannst dein Budget u. a. für steueroptimierte Angebote wie den steuerfreien Sachbezug, einen Internet-Zuschuss, den Mobilitäts-Zuschuss, eine Erholungsbeihilfe oder einen KITA-Zuschuss nutzen.
